text:
maya: heads up — we saw a spike this morning where eu-west latency jumped and the region chooser oscillated between eu and us-west for a subset of tenants. want to propose a different selector: slope-based region pick + soft failover to reduced-capacity model variants. thoughts?

alex: can you sketch the slope metric? is it just delta(latency)/delta(time) or something fancier?

maya: basic idea: compute EWMA of recent rtt and its derivative. if slope > threshold for Xs, mark region 'degrading' and steer new requests to next candidate. avoid switching back unless slope becomes negative for a cooldown window. this reduces flip-flopping.

alex: makes sense. need to tie to tenant tier though — premium customers should get sticky affinity even during small slopes, while free tiers can be aggressively steered.

sophia: agree. also add a model-variant soft-fail policy: when region is degraded, try smaller or quantized variant in the same region before cross-region. cheaper and lower latency risk. fallback order: local-quant -> local-small -> remote-standard.

maya: exactly. UX ask for console: expose three knobs: slope_threshold_ms/s, cooldown_s, and variant_deescalation_order. plus a tenant override toggle.

alex: implementation note — the routing API will need a new field on DecisionContext: `region_slope` and `last_slope_ts`. we can keep it opaque string or numeric. SDK surface? maybe numeric float.

mike: watch out for cache/WARM issues. if we switch variants often we lose KV cache benefits. need a penalty when variant change rate > N to avoid thrashing. maybe hysteresis on variant changes.

dave: for telemetry/dashboarding let's add these charts to the per-tenant page: 1) region_slope (EWMA) 2) region_switch_count (1h/24h) 3) variant_change_rate 4) cross-region p99 latency. also add an incident alert when region_switch_count spikes > threshold.

ops: quota interaction: when tenant is over quota and we route them cross-region, billing/limits should reflect remote egress. need to surface expected extra charge in the console before steering — or prevent steering for billing-sensitive tenants.

maya: good point. proposal: routing policy evaluates `billing_sensitive` flag in tenant metadata. if true, prefer local variant (possibly degraded) rather than cross-region. add console checkbox: "prevent cross-region steering for billing-sensitive tenants".

alex: sample policy proto i sketched — dropping as a snippet:```json
{
  "policy_name": "slope_soft_failover_v1",
  "slope_threshold_ms_per_s": 5.0,
  "cooldown_s": 30,
  "tier_overrides": {
    "premium": { "slope_threshold_ms_per_s": 20.0, "allow_cross_region": false },
    "free": { "slope_threshold_ms_per_s": 3.0, "allow_cross_region": true }
  },
  "variant_order": ["local-quant","local-small","remote-standard"],
  "hysteresis": { "variant_change_min_interval_s": 300 }
}
```

sophia: love it. small UX tweak: show a simulated impact panel when toggling these values — estimate p50/p95 token latency and expected extra egress cost based on last 1h traffic profile.

maya: action items: 1) alex + mike to prototype policy evaluation in the routing service (ETA 1 week). 2) dave to add telemetry hooks and dashboard tiles (ETA 1 week). 3) product/console: mockup the three knobs + simulate panel (sophia volunteered to mock). 4) ops to list billing-sensitive tenants for testing.

mike: noted. i'll add variant-change rate limiter in runtime and ensure kv cache warming has a backoff.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for routing-service branch slope-failover-proto on prod-canary (cf: deploy/2024-03-15T07:40Z) :rocket:

ops: I'll provide the tenant list and run a small traffic replay against canary tomorrow.

dave: will wire up dashboards to the canary logs + metric stream. also adding a derived metric `slope_violation_count`.

maya: thanks all. ping me here with any blockers. if canary looks good we can roll to staged and then full rollout with console defaults conservative for premium tenants. :eyes:

alex: +1, prefer gradual rollout and an A/B flag in console. :shipit:
